Let

\[
f(p)=3\cdot 16^p+3\cdot 8^p-64\cdot 4^p+61\cdot 2^p+42\cdot 6^p
-4\cdot 12^p-18\cdot 3^p-9\cdot 9^p-7 .
\]

The supremal negative type is the first positive zero of this exponential polynomial:

\[
\wp \approx 0.7921831449751005.
\]

More precisely,

\[
\wp=\text{the unique root of }f(p)=0\text{ in }(0,1).
\]

Sketch of the computation. The 14 triangulations split under the dihedral action into three orbits:

- 6 fan triangulations,
- 6 mixed triangulations,
- 2 alternating triangulations.

For an orbit-constant coefficient vector taking values \(a,b,c\) on these three orbits, the zero-sum condition is

\[
6a+6b+2c=0,\qquad c=-3a-3b.
\]

Writing \(x=2^p,\ y=3^p\), the conditional quadratic form on the \((a,b)\)-plane has matrix entries

\[
H_{00}=-36-24y+18x+18x^2,
\]

\[
H_{01}=-6-6y-24x+18x^2,
\]

\[
H_{11}=6+12y-66x+24x^2.
\]

Thus its determinant is

\[
36f(p).
\]

The remaining Fourier blocks under rotation are strictly negative at this first zero and remain negative up to it, so the first loss of conditional negative definiteness occurs exactly when

\[
\det H=0.
\]

At \(p=\wp\), this determinant has a simple zero while the other blocks are nonsingular negative, so the equality space is one-dimensional. Explicitly, it is spanned by the orbit-constant vector with

\[
(a,b,c)=\left(1,\,-\frac{H_{00}}{H_{01}},\,-3-3\left(-\frac{H_{00}}{H_{01}}\right)\right)_{p=\wp}.
\]

Numerically this is proportional to

\[
(1,\,-1.031140859,\ 0.093422577)
\]

on the three orbit types above.

Therefore

\[
\boxed{(\wp,\dim E)=\left(\wp,1\right)}
\]

where \(\wp\) is the unique root in \((0,1)\) of \(f(p)=0\), approximately \(0.7921831449751005\).
